name: Agent developer
oneLine: Builds shopping or API-consuming agents; wants clear SDKs, errors and test modes.
goals: Pay for an API or a tool call inside the agent loop with one SDK call, over HTTP, MCP or A2A.
Handle a 402 response, sign the payment and retry without hand-coding each scheme or header format.
Keep a wallet or spend cap for the agent that bounds the worst case when a prompt goes wrong.
Run a full checkout against a merchant in a test mode with fake money and a predictable set of error codes.
Register the agent once (an ERC-8004 agentId, a Visa or Mastercard agent registration, a Web Bot Auth key) and reuse that identity across merchants.
Get machine-readable errors with a resolution hint instead of a free-text message.
pains: x402 V1 and V2 use different header names, body shapes and network identifiers, and both are live in the wild.
Every merchant and surface pair needs its own bearer-token onboarding under ACP, so one agent needs many secrets.
Facilitators and merchants return different errors for the same failure (expired validBefore, wrong payTo, insufficient balance), and sandboxes rarely let you inject those failures.
Payment and service delivery are not atomic. The payment can settle and the resource call can still fail.
AP2 mandates, Verifiable Intent and SPT allowances all express spending constraints, but each has its own schema, signing algorithm and lifetime.
Most ERC-8004 registrations are placeholders, so a lookup proves little about whether a counterparty agent works.
decisions: Which protocol stack to support first (x402 or MPP for pay-per-call, ACP or UCP for checkout, AP2 for user authorization) and which rail (USDC on Base, Tempo, cards via SPT, Lightning).
Where the agent's keys live: an in-process wallet, a hosted agentic wallet, or a delegation from the user's wallet under ERC-7715 or ERC-7710.
What spend controls to hard-code in the agent versus leave to the facilitator or the issuer.
Which facilitator to trust for verify and settle, and what to do when it is down.
How much of the payment trail to log and expose to the user.
